title: Here Documents & Here Strings 📝
description: Feed multiline text or single strings directly into commands without temporary files.

slides.title: What is a Here Document? 📄
slides.content:
## `<<` – Inline Multiline Input

A **here document** allows you to pass a block of text directly to a command's stdin.

```bash
command <<DELIMITER
line 1
line 2
DELIMITER
```
All text until the delimiter appears is fed to the command. Common delimiter: `EOF`.

slides.title: Here Doc Basic
slides.content: Use cat to display a block of text:
slides.codeSnippet:
cat <<EOF
Hello,
This is a here document.
EOF

quizData.question: What does the delimiter after `<<` do?

options.text: It marks the end of the input block

quizData.explanation: The delimiter indicates where the input ends; it must appear on a line by itself.

slides.title: Quoting Delimiters & Indentation 🧼
slides.content:
## Control Expansion and Whitespace

- If the delimiter is quoted (e.g., `'EOF'`), variable expansion and command substitution are **disabled** inside the here document.
- Use `<<-` (with a dash) to strip leading **tab** characters – useful for indentation in scripts. (Spaces are not stripped.)

slides.title: Quoted vs Unquoted
slides.codeSnippet:
name="Cybron"
cat <<EOF
Hello $name
EOF
cat <<'EOF'
Hello $name
EOF

quizData.question: To prevent variable expansion in a here document, you must ___ the delimiter.
quizData.explanation: Quoting the delimiter (single or double quotes) disables expansion.

slides.title: Here Strings: `<<<` 🧵
slides.content:
## Single Line Inline Input

A **here string** sends a single string (or a variable) as stdin:

```bash
command <<< "some text"
command <<< "$variable"
```
It's a compact alternative to `echo "text" | command` that avoids a subshell.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Use here docs to generate configuration files or SQL queries inside a script, avoiding temporary files and external `echo` chains.
